# 1.2.70 - five long files split, nothing they do changed

The sixteenth stage on the way to 1.3.0 (E34), released on its own. It
splits five long files of the module by role - the murder incident,
the fog, the projects and their tray, and a Call's effects - into eleven
new files, and changes nothing the module does. The five old files stay,
and every name they offered at 1.2.69 still answers from them. It
prepares the stages that change the incident, the fog, the projects and
the Calls next.

## Before installing

1. **No new migration step, no new setting and no new text.** Nothing
   in the language files, the module's templates, or its manifest and
   styles (but their version stamps) changed.
2. **A macro or another module that imports the module's files keeps
   working.** `scripts/murder.mjs`, `fog.mjs`, `projects.mjs`,
   `projects-ui.mjs` and `call-effects.mjs` still export every name they
   exported at 1.2.69, each the same function; a name that moved is
   re-exported from the file that holds it now (checked on each commit
   that moves code and on the whole stage at once). `game.drpg` offers
   the same functions.
3. **A world loads eleven more script files**: 118 reached from the
   module's entry by static import, where 1.2.69 had 107 (counted in the
   repository). How much longer a world takes to load at a table is not
   measured yet.

## At the table

- **Nothing changes.** In the harness, every test of the suite reads the
  same as on 1.2.69: the same tests, in the same order, with the same
  results and the same reasons, and every scenario the same checks.

## Changed

For whoever reads or changes the code. `CLAUDE.md`'s "Where the code
lives" names each file's role; the GM handbook's file lines for the fog,
the projects and the murder engine name the new files beside the old
ones.

- **The murder incident.** `murder.mjs` holds no code now. The incident's
  record - its world half and its cast, each participant's copy, the
  queue and the Blackened register - is in `incident-store.mjs`, the one
  new file that listens on the socket; the rules of the three stages in
  `murder-rules.mjs`; the Murder window and the GM's tracker in
  `murder-ui.mjs`.
- **The fog.** `fog.mjs` keeps the layer, the discovery ledger, the
  dissolve and the raster. Its shape math is in `fog-geometry.mjs`, which
  holds no state; the doorways in `fog-doorways.mjs`; the reveal and the
  room's outline in `fog-reveal.mjs`; the map's checks and `whatIsHere`
  in `fog-diagnostics.mjs`.
- **Projects.** A project's secret fields and who may see it are in
  `projects-secrecy.mjs`; what the countdown tray draws is in
  `projects-tray.mjs`.
- **Calls.** The windows a Call opens to pick what it is pointed at are
  in `call-pickers.mjs`; sealed rooms, the silence and the chain, and the
  called assembly in `call-world.mjs`.
- **A checker for moves.** `node tools/moved-only.mjs <base> [<head>]`
  reads a commit that moves code and is red unless every line moved, was promoted to an
  export, is an import or a file's header; every top-level statement of the
  files it touches has the same tokens at both ends, comments aside; every
  name read means what it meant; the old files export the same
  declarations, and no name a file stops exporting is still imported; and
  every function a test reads by name, as a table's key or through the
  bridge's and R290's crawls is cut the same. Its 40 planted pairs run as
  `node tools/check.mjs moves`, and in CI with the other checks.
- **The lint refuses an assignment to an imported name**
  (`no-import-assign`): a file split can turn a variable another part of
  the file wrote into an import, which would only fail when it runs.

## Known gaps

- The move checker reads text and scope, not what the code does when it
  runs. It does not count tier 0's read of every function of
  `character.mjs` (no commit of this stage moves one), nor a crawl's reach
  through an arrow function; of the 4040 `import()` calls it reads
  (counted before the second review's fixes), 30 are in a form whose
  names it does not read, and it counts them.
- The fog and the Murder window are not yet tried at a table on this
  version (the audit's live checks, section 9.2, items 135 and 136).

## Checked

- The headless suite, run as `npm test` on this release's code (commit
  2c7ad5a: the tree that ships but for the version stamps, these notes,
  the stage registry's row and the local gate's record): 937 passed, 0
  failed, 17 skipped, the same tests with the same results, in the same
  order and with the same reasons as 1.2.69's; no test was added. The
  scenarios: 18 of 18 green, each with the same checks as on 1.2.69;
  72's three expected reds stand (S17-31 until E43, a Foundry limit,
  S17-64 until E60). The lint, the checks and the gate's self-test were
  green in the same run. The whole chain read the same at three
  checkpoints of the stage before this one: after the fog's last move,
  after the first review's fixes and after the last text commit.
- Each commit that moves code was checked by the move checker, and so
  was the whole stage at once, from 1.2.69 to this release's code with
  comments allowed to change: green on all eight parts. Each test that
  reads moved code by its file's name was pointed back at the old file
  once and failed.
- The Polish file's prose check: 497 of 497 strings covered, missing 0,
  extra 0.
- Before this commit, the stage's six verify sentences and three doneWhen
  clauses were each matched to the check that answers them. One clause,
  that later stages edit the new files, is a promise no check can answer
  now; the stage's own count of the files that import `murder.mjs` (19)
  measured 36 (25 of them the module's own files, each with the same code
  at 1.2.69 and now, comments aside).
- An independent review in two rounds (whether the change is correct and
  whether its checks measure what they claim); its findings were fixed in
  two commits after each round.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet: the fog at a table, its console
  reports answering as on 1.2.69 and the world's load time; the Murder
  window, the tracker's "ask again", a crisis action, Stage 6 and a
  betrayal offer (LIVE-E34-01 and 02). The local release gate needs a
  local Foundry v14 and did not run for this release.
